grades.reason: Describes the mtval2 CSR and the information it records on traps into M-mode. It does not explain why a VMM must intercept privileged guest instructions.
Covers HFENCE.GVMA/HFENCE.VVMA operand semantics and flush behavior. It does not address why privileged guest instructions need interception for trap-and-emulate.
Describes the vsatp register, which hardware substitutes for satp when V=1. That is hardware-assisted virtualization of a CSR, not the rationale for trapping and emulating privileged instructions.

grades.quote: Attempts to execute HFENCE.VVMA or HFENCE.GVMA when V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception, while attempts to do the same in U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
grades.reason: Gives one concrete example of privileged guest instructions causing exceptions when run with V=1. This is the trap mechanism that hands control to the hypervisor. It does not state the underlying reason (isolation, resource control, emulation of privileged state), so it is only auxiliary.
